verdict.summary: You can create an app and connect your own account in minutes, and install it privately in up to 10 accounts, or up to 25 accounts as an unlisted Marketplace app, with no review. Unlimited installs need Marketplace listing, which is a manual review plus several requirements, including three active unaffiliated installs.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for private use; 2-5 days for a listing submission
verdict.approval_wait: none for private or unlisted installs; about 10 business days for the initial listing review, with the full feedback loop up to 60 days

gates.name: Developer account app / developer test accounts
gates.unlocks: Create the app and connect your own account or developer test accounts.
limits: You must sign HubSpot's Acceptable Use Policy via Begin publishing on the Distribution tab before installing outside developer test accounts
Static token apps: one standard account plus up to 10 developer test accounts

gates.name: Private distribution / unlisted Marketplace app (pre-listing)
gates.unlocks: Other customers can install the app: up to 10 allowlisted accounts via private OAuth distribution (100 for Solution Partners), or up to 25 installs as an unlisted Marketplace OAuth app.
limits: Private distribution: 10 accounts (100 for Solution Partners)
Unlisted Marketplace OAuth app: 25 installs until listed
Users see an unverified-app warning and must type an acceptance phrase
The installer must be a Super Admin or hold Marketplace Access permission plus the permissions for the requested scope groups
A Super Admin may need to approve the app for non-admin installs
Only one verified domain per developer account
gates.time_to_reach: Same day to a few days

gates.name: Marketplace listing (and optional certification)
gates.unlocks: Unlimited installs and removal of the unverified warning after listing. Certification is a higher tier.
limits: Initial review aims for 10 business days; the feedback loop is up to 60 days
Only one app can be submitted at a time
Certification needs 60 active installs, a demo video and a security assessment, and lasts 2 years
A failed certification can be reapplied for after 6 months
gates.time_to_reach: About 2-10 weeks for listing; certification needs 6+ months of listing first

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Sign up for a developer account, which is separate from a regular HubSpot account. Create developer test accounts for testing.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Create an app in the developer account, either through the Developer Platform UI or Projects/CLI with an app-hsmeta.json file. Choose OAuth as the auth type.

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: In the app's Auth settings, add the redirect URL and declare scopes as required, conditionally required or optional. Request only the scopes you use. The redirect URL must be https in production and a domain, not an IP address. Localhost may use http.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A required scope missing from the authorize URL's scope parameter causes an error on the authorize page

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: Copy the client ID and client secret from the Auth tab and put them in your Composio auth config. The secret can be rotated there if it is compromised, which invalidates the old one.

steps.title: Accept the policy and connect your own account
steps.detail: On the Distribution tab click Begin publishing and sign the Acceptable Use Policy. Then run the authorize flow against https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize and install in a test account. The app only shows as a Connected App once the token exchange succeeds. Use Development > Monitoring > Logs (OAuth tab) to debug.
gotchas: Access tokens expire (30 minutes per one guide; see expires_in) and must be refreshed with the refresh token

steps.title: Choose a distribution mode for other users
steps.detail: Pick private OAuth distribution (10 allowlisted accounts, 100 for Solution Partners) or Marketplace distribution (25 installs before listing). You can switch from private to Marketplace later without breaking existing installs. Make sure installers are Super Admins or hold Marketplace Access permission.
gotchas: Static-token private apps stay at a single standard account
Sensitive scopes can be added directly on private apps, but Marketplace apps must request them from the Ecosystem Quality team

steps.title: Verify a domain (recommended)
steps.detail: Add a domain in the developer account and create the DNS TXT record HubSpot gives you. One verified domain applies to all apps in the account. The unverified-app warning stays until the app is listed or certified.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets
steps.detail: Draft the setup docs, support pages, Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, pricing and the Shared data table that matches the scopes. Allow the HubSpot Crawler user agent on your site. Make sure the app uses a supported platform version, with 2026.03 as the recommended target, and does not use classic CRM cards.

steps.title: Meet listing prerequisites
steps.detail: Use OAuth as the only authorization method. Call the API with the public app ID and client ID attached to the listing. Agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement. Get at least 3 active unique installs from accounts not affiliated with you.
gotchas: Listing apps cannot use sensitive data scopes

steps.title: Submit the listing and wait
steps.detail: Submit one app at a time. The Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing manually, with an initial review aimed at 10 business days. Fix anything they flag. The whole feedback loop should take up to 60 days.
gotchas: Incomplete listings are set to Draft
A second submission while one is pending is automatically rejected

steps.title: Optionally apply for certification
steps.detail: After at least 6 months of listing and 60 active installs, apply for certification. You need a demo video, a verified domain, a security questionnaire and a passed security assessment. Certification is free and valid for 2 years.

requirements.detail: Required via Begin publishing on the Distribution tab before installing outside developer test accounts.
The installer must be a Super Admin or hold Marketplace Access permission, plus the permissions for the requested scope groups.
One per developer account. It is required for certification.
An active install is a production account unaffiliated with you with successful activity in the past 30 days.

requirements.item: Live legal and support URLs, pricing and support contact
requirements.detail: The Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live. Setup docs, install button and support resources must be reachable. Pricing must match your website.
Allow the user agent before submission.

requirements.item: Single OAuth app ID, single use case, supported platform version
requirements.detail: OAuth only. The listing's public app ID and client ID must be used for API calls.
Also, you must not serve restricted industries exclusively.

requirements.item: Certification: 60 installs, demo video, security assessment, 6 months listed
requirements.detail: Also requires a 95% success rate and errors under 5% of daily requests.

scopes.effect: Listing and certification require every requested scope to be used. Remove extras and mark partially used ones as conditional or optional.

scopes.scope: Sensitive Data scopes (sensitive and highly sensitive variants)
scopes.effect: Need an Enterprise account. Marketplace apps must request them from the Ecosystem Quality team and pass compliance checks. Private apps can add them directly. Listed apps and agent tools cannot use them.

scopes.scope: settings.users.write and broad CRM write scopes (Composio defaults)
scopes.effect: The Composio default list is broad. A self-owned app should trim it to what it uses before listing.

blockers.symptom: Install fails or app is over the cap at 25 installs
blockers.cause: Unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps on 2025.2 are capped at 25 installs. Migrated legacy apps over 25 have the cap enforced.
blockers.fix: Get listed, or use private distribution if you need 10 or fewer accounts. Contact HubSpot support for errors.

blockers.cause: A required scope is missing from the scope parameter of the authorize URL.
blockers.fix: Make the URL's scope parameter match the scopes declared in the app's auth settings.

blockers.symptom: Non-admin user cannot install the app
blockers.cause: The user lacks Super Admin or Marketplace Access permission, or a Super Admin has not approved the app.
blockers.fix: Have a Super Admin install it or grant the permissions and approve the app.

blockers.cause: Marketplace OAuth apps get 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account (the certification page says 100). Private apps have per-app burst limits and daily caps.
blockers.fix: Plan for the stricter 100 figure, and batch and back off on requests.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected or set to Draft
blockers.cause: Incomplete fields, unreachable URLs, extraneous scopes, or an unsupported platform version.
blockers.fix: Fix the issues and resubmit. Only one submission can be open at a time.

composio.note: Managed OAuth is fine for testing or a few accounts. Its default scope list is broad. Bring your own HubSpot app for Marketplace listing or certification, because listing is tied to your own public app ID and client ID. Add the Composio callback URL to your app's redirect URLs (inferred).

evidence.claim: Unlisted marketplace OAuth apps are capped at 25 installs until listed.
evidence.quote: Until your app is reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and listed on the Marketplace, you'll be limited to 25 installs.

evidence.claim: Listing needs OAuth only and a single app ID.
evidence.quote: Single HubSpot app ID: your app must authorize API requests with the public HubSpot app ID (and OAuth client ID) associated with your app listing.

evidence.claim: Listing requires 3 active unique installs.
evidence.quote: Active installs are the number of unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization, showing successful app activity within the past 30 days.

evidence.claim: Agreement, restricted industries, no classic CRM cards.
evidence.quote: your app cannot use classic CRM cards, as they are no longer supported as of June 16, 2025.

evidence.claim: Live URLs, pricing and support contact required for listing.
evidence.quote: URLs for your app's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy must be live and up-to-date.

evidence.claim: HubSpot Crawler must be allowed.
evidence.quote: add HubSpot's crawler's user agent, HubSpot Crawler, to the allow list as an exemption prior to submitting your app listing.

evidence.claim: Supported platform version needed for listing.
evidence.quote: Marketplace apps that submit for listing/relisting or certification/recertification must run on a supported Developer Platform version

evidence.claim: Initial review within 10 business days; feedback loop up to 60 days.
evidence.quote: the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team will complete an initial review within 10 business days.

evidence.claim: One submission at a time.
evidence.quote: you can only submit one app at a time for approval.

evidence.claim: Incomplete listings go to Draft; HubSpot may reject.
evidence.quote: failure to meet these requirements will cause your listing to be set to Draft mode only

evidence.claim: Certification requirements including demo video and security questionnaire.
evidence.quote: HubSpot will not review your app unless you submit a demo video as instructed when applying for app certification.

evidence.claim: Install caps by distribution type.
evidence.quote: Marketplace OAuth app prior to listing: can be installed in up to 25 accounts (not including developer test accounts).

evidence.claim: Certification requires a security assessment.
evidence.quote: Pass an assessment for security best practices related to outdated software and various web server vulnerabilities and findings.

evidence.claim: Certification needs 60 active installs and 6 months listed.
evidence.quote: Your app must have at least 60 active, unique installs to qualify for and retain certification.

evidence.claim: 5% error ceiling for certification.
evidence.quote: If you plan on listing your app in the HubSpot Marketplace, it must stay under this 5% limit to be certified.

evidence.claim: Certification is free and valid two years.
evidence.quote: No, we do not charge you a fee to list or certify your apps in the HubSpot Marketplace, nor a fee for installs generated through the HubSpot Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Certification review timing and reapply after six months.
evidence.quote: Should your app not successfully complete the review, you may re-apply in six months.

evidence.quote: Extraneous scopes must be removed.

evidence.claim: Scopes must match the authorize URL scope parameter.
evidence.quote: you'll need to include them in this parameter or the authorization page will display an error.

evidence.claim: Sensitive Data scopes need Enterprise.

evidence.claim: Marketplace apps must request sensitive scopes from Ecosystem Quality.
evidence.quote: you'll need to request access to specific sensitive scopes from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team.

evidence.claim: Private apps can add sensitive scopes directly.

evidence.claim: Begin publishing on the Distribution tab, with Acceptable Use Policy signing.

evidence.claim: Agent tool listings cannot use sensitive scopes.
evidence.quote: at this time, your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: Listed apps must not use sensitive data scopes.
evidence.quote: Your app must not access, request, or use sensitive data scopes.

evidence.claim: 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account.
evidence.quote: each HubSpot account that installs your app is limited to 110 requests every 10 seconds.

evidence.claim: Certification page states 100 requests per 10 seconds.
evidence.quote: Respecting rate limits (i.e. 100 inbound requests every 10 seconds per connected HubSpot account).

open_questions: Refresh token lifetime and rotation behavior were not stated on any official page read.
Whether business verification, a paid subscription or partner enrollment is needed to create a developer account or list an app was not stated.
The rate limit is stated as 110 per 10 seconds on one page and 100 on another; this was not reconciled.
The sensitive-scope request form and its review timeline were not read.
Whether the legacy private app creation cutoff (reported around October 26, 2026 by a third party) has taken effect is unverified.
Whether the demo video is needed for basic listing is unconfirmed; official pages require it for certification.
